whatFailed: GET /api/v2/envelope/{unknown id} correctly answers 404 but its body is the tRPC/OpenAPI envelope {message, code, data}, so the top-level `error` and `statusCode` members that the Getting Started page publishes as "the" v2 error response format do not exist.

docClaim.section: Error Handling > Error Response Format / Common Errors (Envelope not found)

observed: Both steps got HTTP 404 with body {"message":"Envelope could not be found","code":"INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR","data":{"code":"NOT_FOUND","httpStatus":404,"path":"envelope.get","appError":{"code":"NOT_FOUND","message":"Envelope could not be found"}}}. The status assertion in step 1 passed. In step 2 `code` exists (so that assertion passed) but its value is INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, `error` is absent (the reported mismatch) and `statusCode` is absent too. Server log confirms a clean NOT_FOUND AppError: {"status":"error","appError":{"code":"NOT_FOUND","message":"Envelope could not be found"},"path":"envelope.get","msg":"TRPC_ERROR_HANDLER"}. No stack traces, no 500s.
impact: Anyone writing an error handler from the Getting Started page reads err.error and err.statusCode and gets undefined on every tRPC-backed v2 endpoint, so error messages vanish from their integration and 404 handling silently falls through to a generic branch. Product-side rider (not what this step failed on): the top-level `code` is INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR on a 404, so the code taxonomy in common-errors.md is unusable at the top level and callers must dig into data.code.

rootCause.explanation: The doc block is hand-written and describes an envelope the tRPC surface never emits. Every v2 endpoint generated by trpc-to-openapi returns the tRPC error shape: packages/trpc/server/trpc.ts:39-67 builds the body from tRPC's default shape {message, code, data} and only enriches `data` (appError, code, httpStatus) when the cause is an AppError; apps/remix/server/trpc/hono-trpc-open-api.ts:21-33 separately forces the HTTP status to the AppError's mapped status, which is why the status is a correct 404 while the body keys are the tRPC ones. There is no `error` member and no `statusCode` member anywhere on this path. The doc text is also contradicted inside Documenso's own docs: recipients.mdx and fields.mdx (the other two pages this scenario binds) publish the real shape, 'Example Error Response: {"message": "Recipient already exists"}', and documents.mdx, templates.mdx, teams.mdx and common-workflows.mdx use `message` as well. Only first-api-call.mdx and rate-limits.mdx carry the {error, code, statusCode} fiction, and an open contributor PR (#3133) is already rewriting the rate-limits.mdx copy of it into the real {message, code, data:{code, httpStatus, appError}} shape. Two caveats that stop this being 100 percent fiction: the hand-rolled Hono download routes mounted into the same namespace (apps/remix/server/api/download/download.ts:129-141, mounted at apps/remix/server/router.ts:127 as app.route('/api/v2', downloadRoute)) really do return {error, code}, so /api/v2 serves two incompatible error envelopes depending on the handler; and `statusCode` as a body member exists on neither of them.

issues.title: Feedback for “API Reference” V2
issues.note: A user pastes the exact wire envelope this scenario hit: {"message":"Field type mismatch...","code":"INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR","data":{"code":"INVALID_BODY","httpStatus":400,...}}, plus a second one {"message":"Input validation failed","code":"BAD_REQUEST",...,"issues":[...]}. It is filed about a field-type problem, not about the envelope, and it was closed with only the welcome bot comment, no maintainer reply. It is the best public evidence that the real shape is {message, code, data} and that users are confused by the INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR label, but nobody has reported the docs/wire mismatch itself.

colleagueFinding.note: Right scenario, wrong failing mechanism. Finding #5 says the failure is that the error is labeled INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR with the real code one level down. That labeling is real and visible in the evidence, but it is not what this step failed on: the step asserted only that `code` exists, and that assertion passed. The failure is the missing `error` key (and `statusCode`, also absent), which is a documentation bug in first-api-call.mdx, not a product defect. Three further refinements. (1) 'Every API error' is too strong: the top-level code is accurate whenever a real TRPCError is thrown, for example BAD_REQUEST on zod input validation, as issue #2114's second payload shows; it is specifically AppError-derived failures that get relabeled, because tRPC wraps a non-TRPCError cause as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR. (2) The relabeling has a precise, citable root cause the researcher did not name: genericErrorCodeToTrpcErrorCodeMap in packages/lib/errors/app-error.ts:70-111 already carries the correct TRPCError code per app error code, but both of its only two call sites, packages/trpc/server/trpc.ts:59 and apps/remix/server/trpc/hono-trpc-open-api.ts:25, read `?.status` and never `?.code`. The `code` half of that table is dead. That is a one-line-shaped product fix. (3) 'Unreported' needs a caveat: issue #2114 (closed, no maintainer reply) contains the exact envelope, and open PR #3133 is already correcting the same fabricated doc block on rate-limits.mdx.

notes: Two things a maintainer should take away beyond the doc fix. First, /api/v2 currently serves two incompatible error envelopes: the trpc-to-openapi routes return {message, code, data{...}} and the hand-rolled Hono download routes mounted at the same prefix (apps/remix/server/router.ts:127, handlers at apps/remix/server/api/download/download.ts:101-141 and the audit-log, certificate and document variants below it) return {error, code} or a bare {error}. Documenso's own e2e test packages/app-tests/e2e/api/v2/partial-signed-pdf-download.spec.ts:188,218,242 asserts response.code === 'ENVELOPE_COMPLETED' against that second family, so both shapes are intentional and tested; no single 'Error Response Format' section can be right until they converge. Second, the download family is outside the generated OpenAPI document (packages/trpc/server/open-api.ts only feeds appRouter to generateOpenApiDocument), so openapi.documenso.com does not describe those routes or their envelope at all. Suggested doc fix for first-api-call.mdx: replace the Error Response Format block and the three Common Errors examples with the real tRPC shape, and state that the application error code lives at data.code / data.appError.code, not at the top level. Suggested product fix if maintainers prefer to make the docs true instead: use the already present genericErrorCodeToTrpcErrorCodeMap[...].code to construct a TRPCError with the right code so that the top-level code stops reading INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR on a 404. Finally, note the doc snapshot the scenario bound to was fetched from the live docs site, which tracks main, so it already contains the post-v2.16.0 <EnvelopeWarning /> and the 1000 req/min line; that does not affect this claim, which is identical at the tested tag and on main.
